title: Hull Open
lead: The Meridian is in dock with her hull open from frame nine to frame thirty when Ensign Lira Vey's skin goes pale, and the ice sensors catch it a moment later: a faint song, coming through the ring. Yardmother Ilkin gives you the numbers without raising her voice. Closing your hull takes thirty hours. The Choir will be here in eighteen.

gm.truth: A Choir hunting group is coming to the Deepyards. Nobody can be sure why. It may be following the Meridian, it may be something aboard her, or it could be chance, and the GM should tie this to whatever the player has been carrying, such as a choir_core, a recording or a song. It doesn't have to be answered right away. The Long Families have fewer people here than they pretend, in the Hearth Rings and the old ships, and no guns to speak of. The mothballed ships in the Dark Moorings are all kept fueled, and now the captain learns why: they've always been the lifeboats, and there's room on them, because there are so few left to save. The Meridian has one cannon, or two after a refit. There is one real defense, and only the oldest engineers know it: the ice ring itself. Cut the right anchor lines and the ring's inner band comes apart into a cloud of ice and radio-noise thick enough to hide anything from the Choir, for days. It would also destroy the Deepyards forever. There would be no more drydocks for frigates anywhere. It would end a home that's nine generations old, by order of a planet-born adopted child, if the captain is that. And when the ice falls away, everyone will see what the oldest anchor points are bolted to: a First Builder frame, which nobody built, and which the first Families came here to find. Ilkin won't give the order. She says it's for the heir to give.
beats: The clock. Dunn Marrow, at frame nine, starts yelling before anyone has told him anything. Every Veshti rigger in the yard goes silent, then starts moving twice as fast.
What's possible in eighteen hours: half a hull, or a full evacuation of the free ships, or both badly. Ilkin takes the captain to a very old panel and shows them what the anchor lines do.
The first Choir scouts arrive early. They don't attack. They hang at the edge of the ring and listen, and the older Veshti start praying to their ancestors' ships.
The decision, and it has to be now. People who've never left the ice are being carried to ships, and Ensign Pell Asante is told to fly a frigate with a hole in it through a collapsing ice ring.
After. A cloud of ice where the Deepyards used to be, or a ruined yard and survivors, or a burning ring. Ilkin looks at it through a viewport and calls the captain "little one" one last time.
routes: Patch and run: engineering and void_ops to seal enough of the hull to survive a jump, working outside, with the clock running.
Shoot the ice: gunnery, tactics and piloting to bring the ring down in the right order, using the Meridian's guns not on the enemy but on a home of nine generations.
Get them out: leadership and persuasion to get frightened people off ships they've never left, and streetwise or commerce to get every civilian hauler in the ring to carry strangers.
checks: engineering:very_hard to close enough of the hull in eighteen hours
void_ops:hard to work outside in a moving ice field
gunnery:hard to cut the anchor lines in the right order
piloting:very_hard to fly a damaged frigate through the ring
leadership:hard to get a whole people to abandon their home in an afternoon
tactics:moderate to read what the Choir's scouts are doing
fights: choir_drone boarding at the far docks if the evacuation runs late, and choir_hunter as a last resort. A sealed bulkhead or a cloud of ice will stop nearly anything, and flight is always possible.
outcomes: If the ring comes down, the Choir loses the fleet and the Long Families lose everything but their lives. Thousands of Veshti refugees join the fleet, with their skills and their grief, and the galaxy has no more frigate docks. There's also now a bare First Builder frame out there for anyone who cares to look.

If the captain runs and leaves them, the Meridian survives with a half-closed hull, and the Choir takes the Deepyards slowly. Some of the Families are copied, and later someone with a very long stride walks into a cantina wearing a familiar face.
If the captain finds a third way, such as a false signal or a decoy of the Meridian's name, the Deepyards might survive, damaged, at a price that the player should work out for themselves.
Whatever happens, the Long Bet, if it's running, may come due here. The fleet's oldest ships don't all make it out.
gm.rewards: Survival and, if it goes well, thousands of grateful and brilliant Veshti shipwrights in the fleet. The fleet's morale takes a big swing. Ilkin Ao-Vash's old pilot_gloves, given to the captain with no comment.
